test_title: PYST 73: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: On 26 August 2025, a deadly landslide near which pilgrimage site in Reasi district, Jammu & Kashmir, killed dozens and triggered a high-level investigation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishno Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tragic landslide occurred on **26 August 2025** near the world-famous **Vaishno Devi** shrine, which is located in the **Reasi district** of the Union Territory of **Jammu & Kashmir**.
 
• The incident took place on the track leading to the holy cave, specifically affecting the **Himkoti route** or the traditional **Bhavan-Sanjichhat** stretch, causing several casualties and leading to a **high-level investigation** ordered by the administration.
 
• The **Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board (SMVDSB)**, which manages the pilgrimage, immediately suspended the **Yatra** for safety reasons and launched a massive rescue operation involving the **NDRF**, **SDRF**, and local police.
 
• Preliminary reports suggested that the landslide was triggered by heavy rainfall in the **Trikuta Hills**, highlighting the geological vulnerability of the **Himalayan** region during the monsoon and post-monsoon periods.
 
• The **Lieutenant Governor** of **Jammu & Kashmir**, who serves as the Chairman of the **Shrine Board**, announced a committee to probe the causes of the slide and to review the **disaster management** protocols in place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vaishno Devi Temple:**
 
 
• Located at an altitude of approximately **5,200 feet**, the shrine is situated in the **Trikuta Mountains** near **Katra**.
 
• It is one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in **India**, attracting millions of devotees annually. The base camp for the trek is **Katra**, located in the **Reasi district**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context of Reasi:**
 
 
• The **Reasi district** is home to significant landmarks including the **Chenab Bridge**, the world’s highest railway bridge, and the **Shiv Khori** cave.
 
• The region is characterized by steep slopes and sedimentary rock formations, making it susceptible to **landslides** and **soil erosion** during intense weather events.
 
 
 
• **Other Pilgrimage Sites Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Amarnath Cave:** Located in the **Anantnag** district of **Jammu & Kashmir** at a much higher altitude of **12,756 feet**. It is famous for the natural **Ice Lingam**.
 
• **Hemkund Sahib:** A prominent **Sikh** pilgrimage site located in the **Chamoli district** of **Uttarakhand**, dedicated to **Guru Gobind Singh**.
 
• **Shankaracharya Temple:** An ancient temple dedicated to **Lord Shiva** located on the **Gopadari Hill** in **Srinagar**, **Jammu & Kashmir**.
 
 
 
• **Safety and Mitigation Measures:**
 
 
• The **SMVDSB** has previously installed **wire mesh** and **retaining walls** along the track to prevent falling stones.
 
• Advanced **Weather Forecasting** systems and **CCTV monitoring** are used to track real-time conditions on the **13 km** trek from **Katra** to the **Bhavan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disaster Response:** The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** is the specialized body constituted under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, to deal with such emergencies in **India**.
 
• **Investigation Scope:** The **high-level investigation** typically involves geologists from the **Geological Survey of India (GSI)** to study the stability of the slopes and recommend long-term safety measures like **slope stabilization** and **tunneling**.
 
• **Impact on Pilgrimage:** The **Vaishno Devi Yatra** is a major economic driver for the **Union Territory**, supporting thousands of livelihoods in **Katra** and surrounding areas; hence, safety is a top priority for the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
